text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 2.2% today, rebounding after a sharp three-day selloff that had knocked the stock down nearly 8% from mid-September highs. The bounce appears tied to oil price stabilization and tentative signs of geopolitical de-escalation: reports emerged Thursday of potential talks for a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz (a critical oil shipping chokepoint) and a Senate vote on ending the Iran conflict, which had sent crude prices higher earlier in the week. US crude sits at $96.41/barrel, down from the spike that preceded these negotiations.

Refineries remain busy at 94% utilization, but the company faces genuine near-term headwinds. Diesel prices have jumped sharply (national average near $6.51/gallon), and the threat of a diesel export ban—which would restrict refiner sales and potentially force production cuts—looms large as a policy risk. For now, the prospect of reduced geopolitical tension and stable refining margins appear to have arrested the recent decline, though the fundamental uncertainty around trade policy and fuel exports persists.
